【Nguồn: CLINICAL BURN FIRST AID PROTOCOL BY ANATOMICAL REGION & MEDICAL TRIAGE】

# CLINICAL BURN FIRST AID PROTOCOL BY ANATOMICAL REGION & MEDICAL TRIAGE
> **Clinical Standards & Frameworks Applied:**
> - **%TBSA Assessment:** Prof. Le The Trung's **1, 3, 6, 9, 18 Rule** (National Institute of Burns - Le Huu Trac, Vietnam).
> - **Severity & Triage Scoring:** **ABSI** (Abbreviated Burn Severity Index) & **ABA** (American Burn Association) Specialized Referral Criteria.
> - **Pre-hospital Foundational First Aid:** International resuscitation & emergency standards (WHO, NHS UK, EBA, BBA).

---

## PART 1: %TBSA LOOKUP MATRIX ACCORDING TO PROF. LE THE TRUNG (RULE OF 1, 3, 6, 9, 18)

Unlike Wallace's Rule of Nines (calibrated for Caucasian anthropometry), **Prof. Le The Trung's Rule** is specifically formulated for Vietnamese/Asian physical builds and serves as the clinical gold standard for burn assessment in Vietnam.

| Metric | Anatomical Region | Total Region %TBSA | Anterior (Front) | Posterior (Back) | Clinical Implications |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| **Number 1 (1%)** | **Perineum & Genitalia** | **1%** | 1.0% | — | Critical ABA functional & infection-prone zone |
| | **Neck & Nape** | **1%** | 0.5% (Neck) | 0.5% (Nape) | High risk of airway compromise & scarring |
| | **Palm OR Dorsum of ONE hand** | **1%** | 0.5% (Palm) | 0.5% (Dorsum) | Entire hand (both sides) = 1–2% |
| **Number 3 (3%)** | **Face** | **3%** | 3.0% | — | Aesthetic & sensory vital zone (eyes, nose, mouth) |
| | **Scalp (Hair-bearing area)** | **3%** | 1.5% | 1.5% | Hair often conceals deep burn severity |
| | **Upper Arm (1 side)** | **3%** | 1.5% | 1.5% | From shoulder joint to elbow joint |
| | **Forearm (1 side)** | **3%** | 1.5% | 1.5% | From elbow joint to wrist joint |
| | **Foot (1 side)** | **3%** | 1.5% (Dorsum) | 1.5% (Plantar) | Weight-bearing locomotion surface |
| **Number 6 (6%)** | **Lower Leg (1 side)** | **6%** | 3.0% | 3.0% | From knee to ankle joint |
| | **Both Buttocks** | **6%** | — | 6.0% (3% each) | High risk of fecal contamination |
| **Number 9 (9%)** | **Thigh (1 side)** | **9%** | 4.5% | 4.5% | From groin/hip to knee joint |
| | **Entire Upper Extremity (1 side)** | **9%** | 4.5% | 4.5% | Upper Arm (3%) + Forearm (3%) + Hand (3%*) |
| **Number 18 (18%)**| **Anterior Torso (Chest & Abdomen)**| **18%** | 18.0% | — | Chest 9% + Abdomen 9% |
| | **Posterior Torso (Back & Buttocks)**| **18%** | — | 18.0% | Upper/Lower Back 12% + Buttocks 6% |
| | **Entire Lower Extremity (1 side)** | **18%** | 9.0% | 9.0% | Thigh (9%) + Lower Leg (6%) + Foot (3%) |

> **In-App Dynamic TBSA Calculation Formula:**
> $$\text{Actual } \%TBSA = (\text{Standard } \%TBSA \text{ of Anatomical Region}) \times (\% \text{ Area Involved in that Region})$$
> *(Example: Burn on one forearm [3% TBSA], blister/erythema covers 40% of the forearm $\rightarrow \%TBSA = 3\% \times 40\% = 1.2\%$).*

---

## PART 2: ABSOLUTE OVERRIDING TRIAGE RULES (TRIAGE MATRIX)

Regardless of how small the calculated %TBSA is, the casualty **MUST BE IMMEDIATELY CLASSIFIED AS SEVERE (EMERGENCY DISPATCH / HOSPITALIZATION)** if ANY of the following criteria are met:
1. **Suspected Inhalation Injury / Hot Toxic Gas Inhalation:** Trapped in enclosed-space fire, singed nasal hairs, hoarseness, stridor, carbonaceous sputum.
2. **Full-Thickness Burns (3rd Degree):** Leathery, waxy white or charred black appearance, painless due to destroyed nerve endings.
3. **Burns to Critical Functional / Aesthetic Zones (ABA Criteria):** Face, Hands, Feet, Perineum / External Genitalia, Major Articulations (Joints).
4. **Circumferential Burns:** Full ring burns around the neck, chest, or extremities $\rightarrow$ Immediate risk of compartment syndrome, ischemic amputation, or mechanical asphyxiation.
5. **High-Voltage Electrical or Concentrated Chemical Burns.**
6. **Vulnerable Demographics:** Children $< 5$ years old, elderly $> 60$ years old, or patients with pre-existing cardiopulmonary disease, diabetes, or renal failure.

---

## PART 3: UNIVERSAL 4-STEP FOUNDATIONAL FIRST AID (MANDATORY BEFORE REGIONAL PROTOCOLS)

Before navigating into specific body parts, emergency responders or bystanders must execute the foundational 4-step sequence:

- **Step 1 — STOP (Extinguish Heat Source):** Evacuate victim from immediate danger. If clothing is on fire, enforce **Stop, Drop and Roll**, or smother flames with a clean wool blanket/heavy coat. Disconnect power sources immediately.
- **Step 2 — COOL (Irrigate with Running Water for 20 Minutes):** Immediately irrigate the burn under gentle, running tap water (**15–25°C / 59–77°F**) continuously for **20 minutes**. Most effective within the first 30 minutes, beneficial up to 3 hours post-injury. Never submerge entire body in cold water.
- **Step 3 — REMOVE (Constrictive Items & Constriction Relief):** Swiftly remove rings, watches, bracelets, anklets, belts, footwear, and tight clothing before tissue edema develops. **Cut clothing around adherent materials; NEVER forcefully rip off fabric embedded in the wound.**
- **Step 4 — COVER (Sterile Protective Barrier):** Cover the burn with clean food-grade plastic cling film laid smoothly in flat layers along the limb, or apply non-adherent sterile gauze. **Do not wrap circumferentially, do not tape tightly.**

---

## PART 4: DETAILED FIRST AID PROTOCOLS: 9 ANATOMICAL REGIONS × 3 SEVERITY LEVELS

---

### REGION 1: HEAD – FACE – NECK
- **%TBSA (Prof. Le The Trung):** **7%** total (Face: 3% | Scalp with hair: 3% | Neck/Nape: 1%).
- **Clinical Hazards:** Upper airway edema (stridor, laryngeal spasm), permanent corneal scarring/blindness, severe psychological impact from cosmetic deformity, neck contracture.

#### Level 1: Mild (Superficial / 1st Degree Erythema)
- **Calculated Burn Extent:** $< 1\%$ TBSA (small localized redness on cheek, forehead, or nape).
- **Clinical Signs:** Flushed red skin, mild burning sensation, dry surface, **zero blisters**, eyes clear without scleral injection, normal voice pitch, breathing calm and non-labored.
- **Real-World Scenarios:** Hot steam from rice cooker nozzle; light hot soup splatter on cheek; mild sunburn after outdoor exposure.
- **Step-by-Step Protocol:**
  - **Step 1 (Source Isolation):** Immediately step away from steam vents, boiling pots, or intense sunlight.
  - **Step 2 (Local Cooling):** Apply a clean cloth soaked in cool tap water gently over the flushed area; re-soak and replace frequently for 15–20 minutes. Alternatively, allow gentle running tap water to cascade over the area. Avoid rubbing.
  - **Step 3 (Remove Jewelry):** Remove earrings, necklaces, spectacles, or hairclips to eliminate pressure points.
  - **Step 4 (Expose to Air):** Leave the facial skin exposed to room air. Do not bandage or tape.
- **Bystander/Family Support:** Reassure the victim. For infants and toddlers, gently hold their hands to prevent scratching the sensitive, stinging skin.
- **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN (DO NOT DO):**
  - ⛔ DO NOT apply ice cubes directly to the face (triggers intense vasoconstriction, frostbite, and secondary ischemic necrosis).
  - ⛔ DO NOT apply toothpaste, turmeric, egg whites, lard, cooking oil, or commercial cosmetic creams.
  - ⛔ DO NOT vigorously rub or scrub the skin.
- **Medical Disposition:** Home care and monitoring. Maintain oral hydration.

---

#### Level 2: Moderate (Partial-Thickness / 2nd Degree Blisters)
- **Calculated Burn Extent:** $1\% - 3\%$ TBSA (blisters on cheek, chin, or neck; airway unobstructed).
- **Clinical Signs:** Tense fluid-filled bullae (blisters) containing straw-colored serum on cheeks, chin, or neck; base is weeping red and acutely painful; periorbital edema without eyelid adhesion; voice clear, no respiratory distress.
- **Real-World Scenarios:** Splattering boiling oil from a frying pan onto face and neck; thermos hot water spilling onto chin.
- **Step-by-Step Protocol:**
  - **Step 1 (Remove Constrictions):** Gently remove earrings, spectacles, chokers, and neck chains immediately before soft tissue edema expands.
  - **Step 2 (Continuous Irrigation):** Direct a gentle, smooth stream of cool tap water over the facial burns continuously for 20 minutes. If boiling fluid contacted the eye: hold eyelids wide open and irrigate under low-pressure clean water for at least 15 minutes.
  - **Step 3 (Intact Blister Protection):** Keep all blister roofs completely intact. Drape a moist, sterile non-adherent gauze lightly over the wound to shield from dust.
  - **Step 4 (Anti-Edema Positioning):** Position the patient upright ($90^\circ$) or elevate head on pillows at $30–45^\circ$ to minimize facial and laryngeal edema. Unbutton and loosen shirt collars completely.
- **Bystander/Family Support:** Provide a wide-brimmed hat to shield from sun and airborne particulates during transport. Ensure victim does not pick at or puncture blisters.
- **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN (DO NOT DO):**
  - ⛔ DO NOT wrap circular bandages around the neck (expanding cervical edema will compress the trachea and trigger fatal mechanical asphyxia).
  - ⛔ DO NOT pop or de-roof blisters.
  - ⛔ DO NOT apply ophthalmic ointments or home remedies into burned eyes or open wounds.
- **Medical Disposition:** Facial burns represent a critical aesthetic area per ABA criteria. Transport to an emergency department or specialized burn unit on the same day for sterile dressing and contracture prevention.

---

#### Level 3: Severe (Full-Thickness / Inhalation Injury — Critical Life Threat)
- **Calculated Burn Extent:** Any full-thickness facial burn OR burn associated with smoke/hot toxic fume inhalation regardless of %TBSA.
- **Clinical Signs (1 sign suffices for Severe classification):** Leathery, waxy white or blackened charred facial skin; singed eyelashes, eyebrows, and nasal vibrissae; soot deposits around nares/oropharynx or carbonaceous sputum; hoarseness, brassy cough, audible inspiratory stridor, gasping; severe swollen closed eyelids; circumferential neck burn; history of closed-space confinement in fire.
- **Real-World Scenarios:** Flash fire from mini-gas canister explosion; apartment building fire entrapment; industrial steam boiler explosion at close proximity.
- **Step-by-Step Protocol:**
  - **Step 1 (CALL EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES 115 / 911):** Dispatch ambulance immediately. State clearly: *"Severe facial and neck burn with high suspicion of acute inhalation injury and threatened airway"*.
  - **Step 2 (Airway Positioning & Decompression):** Sit patient upright at $90^\circ$ or high-Fowler’s ($45^\circ$). Use heavy trauma shears to cut away neckties, collared shirts, and scarves immediately.
  - **Step 3 (Gentle Cooling & Eye Irrigation):** If patient is conscious, apply cool, moist compresses to face. If eyes are gummed shut by soot, flush gently with normal saline $0.9\%$.
  - **Step 4 (Hypothermia Prevention & Warmth):** Wrap patient’s body from chest down in clean, warm dry blankets (critical to prevent trauma-induced hypothermia).
- **Bystander/Family Support:** Monitor respiratory rate and effort every 2 minutes. If airway obstructs or patient stops breathing: begin immediate Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR).
- **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN (DO NOT DO):**
  - ⛔ STRICTLY FORBIDDEN to place plastic cling film over the face (causes immediate, fatal suffocation).
  - ⛔ DO NOT circumferentially tape or bandage the neck.
  - ⛔ DO NOT offer oral fluids, water, or milk (induces aspiration and compromises emergency endotracheal intubation).
- **Medical Disposition:** **IMMEDIATE RESUSCITATION & CRITICAL CARE TRANSFER.** Rapid transport via EMS equipped with advanced airway capabilities to a tertiary Burn Intensive Care Unit (ICU).

---

### REGION 2: UPPER ARMS & FOREARMS (UPPER EXTREMITIES)
- **%TBSA (Prof. Le The Trung):** Each upper limb = **9%** total (Upper Arm: 3% [Front 1.5%, Back 1.5%] | Forearm: 3% [Front 1.5%, Back 1.5%] | Hand: 3%).
- **Clinical Hazards:** Circumferential burns leading to upper extremity compartment syndrome (radial/ulnar artery occlusion); flexion contractures of the elbow joint.

#### Level 1: Mild (1st Degree Superficial)
- **Calculated Burn Extent:** $< 1.5\%$ TBSA (erythema on part of arm or forearm).
- **Clinical Signs:** Uniform redness, warm dry skin, hypersensitivity to light touch, no vesicles or bullae, full elbow and wrist range of motion.
- **Real-World Scenarios:** Touching forearm to hot cookware; molten solder spark landing on bicep.
- **Step-by-Step Protocol:**
  - **Step 1 (Cooling):** Place arm under gentle running tap water for 20 minutes.
  - **Step 2 (Jewelry Removal):** Remove wristwatches, fitbits, and bracelets immediately.
  - **Step 3 (Drying):** Gently pat dry with a soft, clean towel without rubbing.
  - **Step 4 (Protection):** Wear a loose-fitting, soft cotton shirt. Dressings are unnecessary.
- **Bystander/Family Support:** Remind victim to avoid harsh soaps and direct sun exposure for 3–5 days.
- **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN (DO NOT DO):**
  - ⛔ DO NOT apply ice directly to the arm.
  - ⛔ DO NOT smear tiger balm, menthol oils, or toothpaste.
- **Medical Disposition:** Outpatient self-care.

---

#### Level 2: Moderate (2nd Degree, Blisters Present, $< 6\%$ TBSA)
- **Calculated Burn Extent:** $1.5\% - 6\%$ TBSA (covering significant portions of arm/forearm without exceeding 10% total body).
- **Clinical Signs:** Extensive fluid-filled bullae; weeping, mottled red dermis; exquisite pain; early mild swelling of the forearm; moving the elbow causes severe skin stretching pain.
- **Real-World Scenarios:** Boiling water spilling down arm from shoulder to wrist; contact with motorbike exhaust pipe along the forearm.
- **Step-by-Step Protocol:**
  - **Step 1 (Emergency De-constriction):** Strip off watches, fitness bands, and tight sleeves immediately before forearm edema progresses.
  - **Step 2 (20-Minute Irrigation):** Irrigate arm continuously under gentle running cool water for 20 minutes.
  - **Step 3 (Longitudinal Covering):** Lay sheets of clean plastic cling film along the length of the arm (laid flat, not coiled), or cover with sterile non-adherent dressings.
  - **Step 4 (Limb Elevation):** Elevate the affected arm on pillows or suspend in an arm sling above heart level to facilitate venous return and reduce throbbing pain.
- **Bystander/Family Support:** Construct a simple triangular bandage sling to immobilize and elevate the forearm during hospital transit.
- **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN (DO NOT DO):**
  - ⛔ DO NOT wrap cling film or elastic bandages spirally/circumferentially around the limb (acts as a venous tourniquet as edema worsens).
  - ⛔ DO NOT rupture blisters.
  - ⛔ DO NOT apply animal grease, plant extracts, or unsterilized ointments.
- **Medical Disposition:** Present to an urgent care center or burn clinic within 24 hours for sterile dressing and assessment.

---

#### Level 3: Severe (Full-Thickness / Circumferential Arm Burn $\ge 6\%$ TBSA)
- **Calculated Burn Extent:** Deep dermal/full-thickness burns $\ge 6\%$ or extensive bilateral arm burns ($> 10\%$ TBSA), OR ANY circumferential limb burn.
- **Clinical Signs:** Dry, leathery, charred black or marble-white arm; complete numbness/anesthesia; burn forms a continuous, uninterrupted ring around the upper arm or forearm; distal forearm is tense and woody; radial pulse weak/absent; fingertips cold, cyanotic, and numb (signs of limb-threatening compartment syndrome).
- **Real-World Scenarios:** Shirt sleeve ignited, creating an engulfing fire around the arm; arm crushed between industrial heated rollers.
- **Step-by-Step Protocol:**
  - **Step 1 (Trauma Shears Excision):** Cut away constrictive sleeves with shears. Cut off rings and bracelets immediately (cut around adherent fabric; do not yank).
  - **Step 2 (Controlled Irrigation):** Irrigate with cool tap water for 10–15 minutes.
  - **Step 3 (Loose Longitudinal Covering):** Drape sterile burn sheets or lay cling film loosely along the extremity.
  - **Step 4 (High Elevation & Systemic Warming):** Prop arm on pillows $\ge 15\text{ cm}$ above heart level. Cover patient’s trunk with a warm dry blanket.
- **Bystander/Family Support:** Call emergency dispatch (115/911). Report: *"Circumferential arm burn with signs of acute compartment ischemia"*.
- **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN (DO NOT DO):**
  - ⛔ ABSOLUTELY FORBIDDEN to wrap constrictive circular dressings around the extremity.
  - ⛔ DO NOT attempt to debride or peel off charred eschar.
  - ⛔ DO NOT administer oral food or fluids (prepare for emergent surgery).
- **Medical Disposition:** **SURGICAL EMERGENCY.** Rapid transfer to a burn surgery unit for urgent emergency escharotomy to release compartment pressures and salvage the limb.

---

### REGION 3: HANDS & FINGERS
- **%TBSA (Prof. Le The Trung):** **Palm OR Dorsum of 1 Hand = 1%** (Both sides of one hand = 2–3%).
- **Clinical Hazards:** **Highest priority functional zone per ABA standards**. High risk of permanent digit web-space fusion (syndactyly) and extensor/flexor tendon destruction leading to permanent disability.

#### Level 1: Mild (1st Degree / Tiny Superficial Spot)
- **Calculated Burn Extent:** $< 0.5\%$ TBSA (isolated small spot on knuckle or fingertip).
- **Clinical Signs:** Localized erythema, mild stinging upon warm contact, intact skin, full active finger flexion/extension.
- **Real-World Scenarios:** Hot grease droplets on hand dorsum; touching hot pot lid briefly.
- **Step-by-Step Protocol:**
  - **Step 1 (Immediate Irrigation):** Hold hand under gentle running tap water for 20 minutes.
  - **Step 2 (Immediate Ring Removal):** Slip off all rings from the affected finger immediately.
  - **Step 3 (Pat Dry):** Dry gently with a clean cloth.
  - **Step 4 (Active Movement):** Leave exposed to air; encourage gentle finger movement.
- **Bystander/Family Support:** Keep hand away from harsh household chemicals for 24–48 hours.
- **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN (DO NOT DO):**
  - ⛔ DO NOT soak hand in fish sauce, vinegar, or salt brine.
  - ⛔ DO NOT smear toothpaste onto fingertips.
- **Medical Disposition:** Outpatient home care.

---

#### Level 2: Moderate (2nd Degree, Blisters on Palm, Dorsum, or Web Spaces)
- **Calculated Burn Extent:** $0.5\% - 2\%$ TBSA of the hand.
- **Clinical Signs:** Clear bullae across palmar or dorsal skin; sausage-like finger edema; excruciating throbbing pain; finger motion causes intense tension and pain.
- **Real-World Scenarios:** Boiling liquid poured over dorsal hand; grabbing hot clothes iron.
- **Step-by-Step Protocol:**
  - **Step 1 (CRITICAL LIFE/LIMB ACTION — REMOVE ALL RINGS WITHIN 5 MINUTES):** All rings must be removed immediately. After 15 minutes of edema, rings act as rigid tourniquets, causing digital gangrene and auto-amputation. (If stuck, use liquid soap lubrication or dental floss wrapping technique).
  - **Step 2 (20-Minute Water Stream):** Irrigate hand under smooth running tap water for 20 minutes.
  - **Step 3 (INTERDIGITAL GAUZE SEPARATION):** Insert clean, damp sterile gauze pads between every single adjacent finger (between thumb-index, index-middle, middle-ring, ring-pinky). **Mandatory goal:** Prevent raw de-epithelialized finger skin surfaces from contacting each other.
  - **Step 4 (Loose Bagging & Position of Function):** Encase entire hand loosely in a clean plastic bag or drape with sterile gauze. Splint hand in the **"Position of Function"** (fingers gently curled as if holding an orange/soft tennis ball), elevated to chest level.
- **Bystander/Family Support:** Assist victim with emergency ring extraction and maintain hand elevation.
- **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN (DO NOT DO):**
  - ⛔ STRICTLY FORBIDDEN to tape or bind burned fingers together without spacers (heals into fused webbed digits / pseudosyndactyly).
  - ⛔ DO NOT pop palmar blisters (thick palmar stratum corneum serves as the best sterile biological dressing).
  - ⛔ DO NOT apply unpasteurized honey, herbal pastes, or raw fats.
- **Medical Disposition:** Mandatory specialist evaluation on the same day. Hand burns require functional splinting and physical therapy follow-up.

---

#### Level 3: Severe (Full-Thickness / Charred Palm / Exposed Tendons)
- **Calculated Burn Extent:** Deep dermal or full-thickness burn to any part of the hand.
- **Clinical Signs:** Hand appears waxy, porcelain-white, or charred black; fingers fixed in rigid extension or flexion claw; total loss of pinprick sensation; fingers cold, mottled dark purple; exposed extensor tendons or phalangeal joints.
- **Real-World Scenarios:** Hand crushed in heated hydraulic press; grasping energized electrical conduit; gasoline fire enveloping the hand.
- **Step-by-Step Protocol:**
  - **Step 1 (Ring Excision):** Cut away constrictive rings using an emergency ring cutter if tissue is already swollen.
  - **Step 2 (Gentle Rinsing):** Gently trickle cool sterile water or saline over hand for 10 minutes.
  - **Step 3 (Sterile Web-Space Padding):** Place moist sterile gauze between all digits.
  - **Step 4 (Sterile Bagging & Severe Elevation):** Place entire hand loosely in a sterile medical plastic pouch. Prop hand $\ge 20\text{ cm}$ above heart level. Keep patient warm with blankets.
- **Bystander/Family Support:** Call emergency dispatch or transport immediately to a dedicated Burn & Hand Reconstruction Trauma Center.
- **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN (DO NOT DO):**
  - ⛔ DO NOT pick away charred skin or pull on exposed tendon fibers.
  - ⛔ DO NOT attempt to forcefully straighten or bend contracted, stiff fingers (ruptures delicate tendons and joint capsules).
  - ⛔ DO NOT administer oral food or drink.
- **Medical Disposition:** **SURGICAL RECONSTRUCTION EMERGENCY.** Requires urgent surgical debridement, fasciotomy, and flap coverage/grafting to preserve manual dexterity.

---

### REGION 4: ANTERIOR TORSO (CHEST & ABDOMEN)
- **%TBSA (Prof. Le The Trung):** **18%** total (Chest: 9% | Abdomen: 9%).
- **Clinical Hazards:** Massive hypovolemic burn shock; circumferential or cuirass chest burn restricting thoracic excursion resulting in asphyxia; hypothermia induced by excessive cooling.

#### Level 1: Mild (1st Degree Superficial, $< 4.5\%$)
- **Calculated Burn Extent:** $< 4.5\%$ TBSA (isolated patches on chest or epigastrium).
- **Clinical Signs:** Speckled red, stinging skin, zero blisters, effortless thoracic respiratory expansion.
- **Real-World Scenarios:** Hot grease popping onto abdomen while cooking; scalding soup splashed onto front shirt.
- **Step-by-Step Protocol:**
  - **Step 1 (Shed Garment):** Gently remove outer shirt.
  - **Step 2 (Cool Moist Compresses):** Place clean towels soaked in cool tap water over the chest/abdomen for 20 minutes, refreshing periodically.
  - **Step 3 (Gentle Drying):** Pat dry with clean towel.
  - **Step 4 (Loose Clothing):** Don a loose, thin cotton T-shirt. Loosen belt.
- **Bystander/Family Support:** Provide a fresh, soft garment.
- **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN (DO NOT DO):**
  - ⛔ DO NOT dump large ice packs across the chest (induces bronchospasm and reflex cardiac arrhythmias).
- **Medical Disposition:** Outpatient self-care.

---

#### Level 2: Moderate (2nd Degree, Blisters Present, $4.5\% - 9\%$)
- **Calculated Burn Extent:** $4.5\% - 9\%$ TBSA (large blistering patches across chest or abdomen, $< 10\%$ total body).
- **Clinical Signs:** Large confluent bullae across chest/abdomen; bright erythematous, weeping dermis; extreme pain; no signs of systemic hypovolemic shock.
- **Real-World Scenarios:** Dropping a boiling soup pot directly onto chest and lap; spilled hot tea saturating front of clothing.
- **Step-by-Step Protocol:**
  - **Step 1 (CUT CLOTHING OFF IMMEDIATELY — DO NOT PULL OVER HEAD):** Use scissors to slit shirt open vertically. Never pull a hot-soaked shirt over the head (drags scalding fabric across face, ears, and eyes). If fabric is fused to the skin: cut around margins and leave adherent fabric intact.
  - **Step 2 (Tempered Moist Cooling):** Apply cool, wet towels to the torso burns for 15–20 minutes.
  - **Step 3 (SIMULTANEOUS TRUNK/LOWER BODY WARMING):** Cover the patient's legs and back with dry blankets to prevent systemic hypothermia.
  - **Step 4 (Drape & Semi-Fowler Positioning):** Lay a sheet of plastic cling film flat across the abdomen/chest. Position patient in a semi-reclining posture ($30–45^\circ$) to ease breathing.
- **Bystander/Family Support:** Transport to hospital via automobile with patient resting comfortably in a reclined seat.
- **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN (DO NOT DO):**
  - ⛔ DO NOT pull scalding clothes upward over the head.
  - ⛔ DO NOT wrap cling film tightly around the entire torso.
  - ⛔ DO NOT intentionally rupture large abdominal blisters.
- **Medical Disposition:** Medical evaluation required within the day for sterile dressings and infection prophylaxis.

---

#### Level 3: Severe (Full-Thickness Torso Burn $\ge 10\% - 18\%$ TBSA / Cuirass Burn)
- **Calculated Burn Extent:** Deep dermal/full-thickness burns $\ge 10\% - 18\%$ TBSA OR circumferential chest burn.
- **Clinical Signs:** Extensive skin sloughing, charred or pearly white rigid thoracic skin ("cuirass burn"); thorax is stiff and cannot expand; tachypnea, shallow gasping respirations, cyanosis; victim shivering uncontrollably, pale, clammy, with rapid thread-like pulse (burn shock).
- **Real-World Scenarios:** Torso clothing caught fire and burned continuously; high-pressure steam explosion in boiler room.
- **Step-by-Step Protocol:**
  - **Step 1 (CALL 115 / 911 IMMEDIATELY):** Report: *"18% extensive torso burn, rigid chest wall restriction, severe respiratory compromise and hypovolemic shock"*.
  - **Step 2 (HYPOTHERMIA WARNING — RESTRICT EXTENSIVE WATER IRRIGATION):** STRICTLY FORBIDDEN to submerge victim in a cold bath or douse with large amounts of cold water. Apply cool moist cloths for a maximum of 5–10 minutes only, then discard immediately to prevent hypothermic cardiac arrest.
  - **Step 3 (Sterile Dry Covering & Maximum Warming):** Cover the open torso wounds with a clean, dry bedsheet. Pile thick, warm dry blankets over the entire patient.
  - **Step 4 (Anti-Asphyxia Positioning):** Position patient in semi-Fowler's position ($30–45^\circ$) with knees slightly flexed to relax abdominal muscles and maximize diaphragm excursion.
- **Bystander/Family Support:** Check carotid/femoral pulses and respiratory rate every 3 minutes until ambulance arrival.
- **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN (DO NOT DO):**
  - ⛔ ABSOLUTELY FORBIDDEN to immerse patient in ice-cold baths.
  - ⛔ DO NOT give oral liquids, water, or milk (induces paralytic ileus vomiting and pulmonary aspiration).
  - ⛔ DO NOT place constrictive binders around the chest.
- **Medical Disposition:** **RESUSCITATIVE TRAUMA TRANSFER.** Immediate ambulance evacuation on a supine stretcher to an Intensive Care Burn Center for urgent chest escharotomy.

---

### REGION 5: POSTERIOR TORSO (BACK & BUTTOCKS)
- **%TBSA (Prof. Le The Trung):** **Back including both buttocks = 18%** (Back: 12% | Both Buttocks: 6% [3% each]).
- **Clinical Hazards:** High risk of fecal contamination/sepsis (buttocks); ischemic pressure necrosis from bed rest; massive insensible fluid evaporation.

#### Level 1: Mild (1st Degree Superficial, $< 4.5\%$)
- **Calculated Burn Extent:** $< 4.5\%$ TBSA of the back.
- **Clinical Signs:** Diffuse pink/red skin, hypersensitivity, no blisters, normal breathing.
- **Real-World Scenarios:** Extensive sunburn across the back after beach visit; scalding shower spray on shoulders.
- **Step-by-Step Protocol:**
  - **Step 1 (Cool Shower Stream):** Stand under a gentle, lukewarm/cool tap shower for 20 minutes.
  - **Step 2 (Drying):** Pat dry gently with a soft cotton bath sheet.
  - **Step 3 (Loose Attire):** Wear very loose, soft cotton clothing.
  - **Step 4 (Prone/Lateral Sleep):** Sleep in prone (on stomach) or lateral position to prevent friction against mattress.
- **Bystander/Family Support:** Provide soft pillows to support side-lying sleep.
- **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN (DO NOT DO):**
  - ⛔ DO NOT scrub back with bath loofahs or sponges.
  - ⛔ DO NOT lie flat on the back under heavy pressure.
- **Medical Disposition:** Home care and rest.

---

#### Level 2: Moderate (2nd Degree, Blisters on Shoulders, Lumbar, or Buttocks)
- **Calculated Burn Extent:** $4.5\% - 9\%$ TBSA of posterior torso.
- **Clinical Signs:** Large serous blisters across shoulder blades, spine, or buttocks; weeping dermal surface; extreme pain; resting back against chairs causes agonizing pain.
- **Real-World Scenarios:** Boiling liquid spilled from top shelf down the spine and buttocks; battery explosion spraying acid/hot fluid onto back.
- **Step-by-Step Protocol:**
  - **Step 1 (Prone Positioning & Garment Cut):** Place patient prone (face down) or on their uninjured side immediately on a clean surface. Cut off shirt.
  - **Step 2 (Posterior Irrigation):** Apply cool, wet towels continuously along the back and buttocks for 20 minutes.
  - **Step 3 (Longitudinal Covering):** Drape sterile non-adherent dressings or lay plastic cling film smoothly down the length of the spine.
  - **Step 4 (Anti-Compression Positioning):** Maintain patient in prone or side-lying position.
- **Bystander/Family Support:** Strictly prevent patient from leaning back against seats or lying supine (body weight will burst all fragile blisters).
- **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN (DO NOT DO):**
  - ⛔ DO NOT allow victim to sit back or lie supine.
  - ⛔ DO NOT pop blister domes.
  - ⛔ DO NOT apply snake fat, lard, or plant leaves onto back wounds.
- **Medical Disposition:** Transport to clinic/hospital lying on side in the rear seat of a car.

---

#### Level 3: Severe (Full-Thickness Posterior Burn $\ge 10\% - 18\%$ TBSA)
- **Calculated Burn Extent:** Deep dermal/full-thickness burn covering entire back and buttocks.
- **Clinical Signs:** Complete loss of epidermis; raw deep purple-red or charred leathery black surface; massive fluid exudation; shivering, hypotension, altered mental status.
- **Real-World Scenarios:** Trapped face-down on burning floor in warehouse fire; motorcycle fuel tank explosion igniting back and buttocks.
- **Step-by-Step Protocol:**
  - **Step 1 (CALL 115 / 911 SPECIFYING STRETCHER TRANSPORT):** Request ambulance with a rigid gurney: *"Severe 18% full-thickness back and buttock burn in hypovolemic shock"*.
  - **Step 2 (Sterile Sheet Placement):** Lay an impeccably clean, dry bedsheet onto the bed. Place patient in prone or lateral position on the sheet.
  - **Step 3 (Cover & Warm Ventral Body):** Drape a dry sterile sheet over the back. Tuck warm blankets securely across patient's chest, abdomen, and front legs.
  - **Step 4 (Airway & Consciousness Check):** Ensure prone posture does not impede respiration; if breathing is labored, position in stable lateral recovery posture.
- **Bystander/Family Support:** Check breathing and pulse every 3 minutes until medical crew arrives.
- **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN (DO NOT DO):**
  - ⛔ ABSOLUTELY FORBIDDEN to position patient supine (on their back).
  - ⛔ DO NOT pour large amounts of cold water over $> 15\%$ posterior burns.
  - ⛔ DO NOT give oral liquids or pain pills.
- **Medical Disposition:** **CRITICAL CARE BURN TRANSFER.** Patient must be transported strictly in prone or lateral position on an ambulance gurney.

---

### REGION 6: BOTH LEGS (THIGHS & LOWER LEGS)
- **%TBSA (Prof. Le The Trung):** Each lower limb = **18%** total (Thigh: 9% [Front 4.5%, Back 4.5%] | Lower Leg: 6% [Front 3%, Back 3%] | Foot: 3%).
- **Clinical Hazards:** Circumferential burn leading to acute lower extremity compartment syndrome; hydrostatic dependent edema causing blister bursting when standing.

#### Level 1: Mild (1st Degree Superficial, $< 4.5\%$)
- **Calculated Burn Extent:** $< 4.5\%$ TBSA (minor splash across calf or thigh).
- **Clinical Signs:** Local erythema, warm tingling, zero bullae, painless unhindered ambulation.
- **Real-World Scenarios:** Brief touch against warm motorcycle exhaust pipe immediately after engine start; hot soup splash on shin.
- **Step-by-Step Protocol:**
  - **Step 1 (Irrigate):** Direct cool tap water stream over the leg for 20 minutes.
  - **Step 2 (Dry):** Pat dry gently.
  - **Step 3 (Loose Shorts):** Wear wide, airy shorts.
  - **Step 4 (Leg Rest):** Sit with leg propped up on an ottoman; minimize excessive walking during day one.
- **Bystander/Family Support:** Encourage leg elevation while sitting.
- **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN (DO NOT DO):**
  - ⛔ DO NOT apply ice packs directly to the leg.
  - ⛔ DO NOT apply hot rub balms or alcohol.
- **Medical Disposition:** Home care.

---

#### Level 2: Moderate (2nd Degree, Blisters Present, Classic: Motorcycle Exhaust Burn)
- **Calculated Burn Extent:** $4.5\% - 9\%$ TBSA of the leg.
- **Clinical Signs:** Linear or oval bulla on calf/thigh filled with serous fluid; surrounding inflammatory erythema; throbbing pain; standing causes instant gravity-driven vascular pooling and agonizing throbbing.
- **Real-World Scenarios:** Direct prolonged contact with scorching motorcycle exhaust pipe; boiling stew dumped over lower limbs.
- **Step-by-Step Protocol:**
  - **Step 1 (EMERGENCY SOCKS & PANTS REMOVAL WITHIN 2 MINUTES):** Remove footwear and immediately use scissors to cut away socks/stockings (synthetic sock fibers retain heat and drive the thermal injury into deep subcutaneous fat).
  - **Step 2 (20-Minute Water Cooling):** Irrigate leg under gentle running tap water for 20 minutes continuously.
  - **Step 3 (STRICT BED REST & ELEVATION — DO NOT WALK):** Rest patient in bed with leg propped on 1–2 pillows above heart level to prevent hydrostatic rupture of blisters.
  - **Step 4 (Sterile Coverage):** Drape sterile non-adherent dressing or lay cling film along the leg.
- **Bystander/Family Support:** Carry or support victim into a vehicle (leg must remain outstretched and elevated horizontally, never hanging downward).
- **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN (DO NOT DO):**
  - ⛔ STRICTLY FORBIDDEN to allow victim to walk on the injured leg (hydrostatic pooling ruptures blisters, inviting virulent soft tissue infection).
  - ⛔ DO NOT pop motorcycle exhaust blisters.
  - ⛔ DO NOT apply lard, crocodile fat, raw turmeric, or concentrated Betadine onto open blister bases.
- **Medical Disposition:** Exhaust burns have an exceptionally high incidence of deep dermal necrosis and hypertrophic scarring. Seek medical treatment on the same day for modern hydrocolloid/silver dressings.

---

#### Level 3: Severe (Full-Thickness / Circumferential Leg Burn $\ge 10\% - 18\%$ TBSA)
- **Calculated Burn Extent:** Deep dermal/full-thickness burn $\ge 10\% - 18\%$ TBSA, OR circumferential leg burn.
- **Clinical Signs:** Pale waxy or charred leathery leg; circumferential burn ring encircling thigh or calf; foot and toes below the burn are swollen, stone-cold, pulseless (dorsalis pedis pulse vanished), and numb (acute compartment syndrome).
- **Real-World Scenarios:** Jeans caught fire and engulfed entire lower extremity; step into pit of burning coals; limb submerged in vat of boiling fluid.
- **Step-by-Step Protocol:**
  - **Step 1 (Trauma Shears Excision):** Rapidly cut away pants, thermal leggings, and shoes.
  - **Step 2 (Moderate Cooling):** Trickle cool tap water over the burn for 10–15 minutes.
  - **Step 3 (Loose Longitudinal Barrier):** Apply clean, unrolled cling film or sterile burn sheets laid flat along the limb.
  - **Step 4 (Immobilization & $30^\circ$ Elevation):** Keep patient strictly supine with both legs elevated $30^\circ$. Wrap upper torso in warm blankets.
- **Bystander/Family Support:** Call emergency dispatch (115/911): *"Full-thickness circumferential leg burn, acute compartment syndrome risk, requires stretcher gurney"*.
- **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN (DO NOT DO):**
  - ⛔ ABSOLUTELY FORBIDDEN to wrap circumferential constrictive elastic bandages around the leg.
  - ⛔ STRICTLY FORBIDDEN to allow the patient to walk even a single step.
  - ⛔ DO NOT give oral food or drinks.
- **Medical Disposition:** **SURGICAL RECONSTRUCTIVE EMERGENCY.** Immediate transfer on a stretcher to a burn surgical center for emergent decompressive escharotomy.

---

### REGION 7: FEET & TOES
- **%TBSA (Prof. Le The Trung):** **Foot (1 side) = 3%** (Dorsum: 1.5% | Plantar/Sole: 1.5%).
- **Clinical Hazards:** **Critical weight-bearing functional zone per ABA criteria**. High risk of long-term disability, intractable plantar ulcers, and toe web-space fusion.

#### Level 1: Mild (1st Degree Superficial, Minor Dorsal Spot)
- **Calculated Burn Extent:** $< 1\%$ TBSA of foot dorsum.
- **Clinical Signs:** Slight erythema on foot dorsum, no blisters, normal toe flexion, painless walking in soft open sandals.
- **Real-World Scenarios:** Few droplets of boiling water splashed onto foot while pouring kettle.
- **Step-by-Step Protocol:**
  - **Step 1 (Water Cooling):** Irrigate foot under gentle cool tap water for 20 minutes.
  - **Step 2 (Remove Shoes/Socks):** Remove footwear immediately.
  - **Step 3 (Dry):** Pat dry gently.
  - **Step 4 (Open Footwear):** Wear loose, open-toe flip-flops; avoid closed shoes.
- **Bystander/Family Support:** Remind victim not to wear tight running shoes for 3 days.
- **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN (DO NOT DO):**
  - ⛔ DO NOT squeeze foot into tight shoes.
  - ⛔ DO NOT smear oily ointments.
- **Medical Disposition:** Home care.

---

#### Level 2: Moderate (2nd Degree, Blisters on Dorsum, Plantar, or Interdigital)
- **Calculated Burn Extent:** $1\% - 3\%$ TBSA of the foot.
- **Clinical Signs:** Tense bullae across foot dorsum or sole; significant dorsal edema; intense pain when foot touches ground; weeping interdigital web spaces.
- **Real-World Scenarios:** Hot broth spilled into boots; charcoal ember trapped under sandal strap.
- **Step-by-Step Protocol:**
  - **Step 1 (SHOE & SOCK EXTRACTION IMMEDIATELY):** Remove shoe and slice away sock with shears immediately.
  - **Step 2 (20-Minute Water Cooling):** Submerge in or stream gentle cool tap water over foot for 20 minutes.
  - **Step 3 (INTERDIGITAL TOE SEPARATION):** Place small strips of damp sterile gauze between every single adjacent toe (preventing toe skin coalescence).
  - **Step 4 (Loose Bagging & 20 cm Elevation):** Encase foot loosely in sterile dressing. Keep patient resting with foot elevated $\ge 20\text{ cm}$ above heart.
- **Bystander/Family Support:** Carry victim or transport in wheelchair. Strictly prohibit foot-to-ground weight-bearing.
- **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN (DO NOT DO):**
  - ⛔ STRICTLY FORBIDDEN to let the patient walk on the burned foot.
  - ⛔ DO NOT permit adjacent burned toes to contact each other without spacers.
  - ⛔ DO NOT pop blisters on the plantar sole.
- **Medical Disposition:** Foot burns are classified as critical functional injuries under ABA criteria. Specialist assessment is mandatory within 24 hours.

---

#### Level 3: Severe (Full-Thickness Plantar Burn / Charred Foot / Sensory Loss)
- **Calculated Burn Extent:** Full-thickness burn involving the foot.
- **Clinical Signs:** Foot is leathery, charred black, or waxy white; complete loss of sensation; exposed extensor tendons or metatarsophalangeal joints; foot is cold, pulseless, and dusky cyanotic.
- **Real-World Scenarios:** Leather boots ignited and incinerated on feet; stepping into lime-slaking pits or deep hot embers.
- **Step-by-Step Protocol:**
  - **Step 1 (Cut Remnants):** Slit and gently remove remaining shoe leather/fabrics.
  - **Step 2 (Gentle Saline Rinse):** Irrigate with cool saline or clean water for 10 minutes.
  - **Step 3 (Interdigital Spacers & Loose Drape):** Insert sterile gauze between toes; drape loose sterile dressing over entire foot.
  - **Step 4 (Immobilization & Elevation $30^\circ$):** Rest foot comfortably, elevated at $30^\circ$. Wrap patient in warm blankets.
- **Bystander/Family Support:** Call emergency dispatch (115/911). Keep victim calm and motionless on stretcher.
- **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN (DO NOT DO):**
  - ⛔ DO NOT attempt to peel away charred skin from the sole of the foot.
  - ⛔ DO NOT allow victim to stand or bear weight.
  - ⛔ DO NOT give oral food or fluids.
- **Medical Disposition:** **SURGICAL LIMB SALVAGE EMERGENCY.** Immediate transfer to a tertiary Burn Reconstruction Unit to prevent deep infection and limb amputation.

---

### REGION 8: MAJOR ARTICULATIONS / JOINTS (ELBOW, KNEE, WRIST, ANKLE, HIP, SHOULDER)
- **%TBSA (Prof. Le The Trung):** Included within parent limb segment, but categorized as **Critical Functional Specialty Zones** (`burn_location = MAJOR_JOINT`) under ABA guidelines.
- **Clinical Hazards:** Highest propensity for **severe hypertrophic scar contracture** resulting in complete joint ankylosis and permanent limb disability.

#### Level 1: Mild (1st Degree Superficial over Joint Apex)
- **Calculated Burn Extent:** $< 1\%$ TBSA.
- **Clinical Signs:** Mild erythema over bony prominence (patella, olecranon), no blisters, unrestricted active joint articulation.
- **Real-World Scenarios:** Skimming knee or elbow against hot metal surface.
- **Step-by-Step Protocol:**
  - **Step 1 (Irrigate 20 Minutes):** Run gentle tap water over the joint for 20 minutes.
  - **Step 2 (Dry):** Pat dry with clean cloth.
  - **Step 3 (Loose Cover):** Cover lightly with clean gauze.
  - **Step 4 (Gentle Range of Motion):** Perform normal gentle joint flexions; do not splint rigidly.
- **Bystander/Family Support:** Advise against scratching the joint apex.
- **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN (DO NOT DO):**
  - ⛔ DO NOT scrub vigorously over bony prominences.
- **Medical Disposition:** Home care.

---

#### Level 2: Moderate (2nd Degree, Blisters across Flexor Crease or Extensor Apex)
- **Calculated Burn Extent:** $1\% - 3\%$ TBSA over joint area.
- **Clinical Signs:** Blisters situated directly across flexor creases (cubital fossa, popliteal fossa) or extensor surfaces (kneecap, elbow tip); joint motion causes severe tearing pain; blisters rupture easily upon bending.
- **Real-World Scenarios:** Boiling soup spilled directly into the popliteal crease or kneecap; exhaust burn across lateral ankle malleolus.
- **Step-by-Step Protocol:**
  - **Step 1 (Cooling):** Irrigate joint under running cool tap water continuously for 20 minutes.
  - **Step 2 (POSITION OF FUNCTION — PHYSIOLOGICAL REST ANGLE):** Support joint in its neutral physiological rest position: **Elbow slightly flexed ($100–110^\circ$)**; **Knee almost fully extended ($5–10^\circ$ of slight flexion only, NEVER bent backwards)**.
  - **Step 3 (Non-Adherent Crease Padding):** Drape a sterile, non-adherent moist gauze pad over the joint folds.
  - **Step 4 (Relative Immobilization):** Rest patient comfortably without forcing joint motion.
- **Bystander/Family Support:** Support the joint in neutral alignment during travel to medical center.
- **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN (DO NOT DO):**
  - ⛔ DO NOT apply rigid, unpadded splints in hyper-flexed abnormal angles.
  - ⛔ DO NOT forcefully flex or snap open burned joints (shreds skin blisters).
  - ⛔ DO NOT pop joint crease blisters.
- **Medical Disposition:** Present to an orthopedic/burn clinic within 24 hours for dynamic splinting and physical therapy prescription to avert debilitating scar contractures.

---

#### Level 3: Severe (Full-Thickness Joint Burn / Exposed Joint Capsule / Tendons)
- **Calculated Burn Extent:** Deep dermal/full-thickness burn traversing a major articulation.
- **Clinical Signs:** Dense, contracted leathery eschar freezing the joint; open joint capsule; exposed glistening white tendons or articular cartilage; excruciating pain or total anesthesia.
- **Real-World Scenarios:** Joint caught between industrial heated compression dies; pants burning fiercely across knee joints.
- **Step-by-Step Protocol:**
  - **Step 1 (Gentle Rinse 10 Minutes):** Trickle cool sterile saline or water over joint for 10 minutes if safe.
  - **Step 2 (Sterile Moist Coverage):** Drape sterile moist gauze gently over exposed articular structures.
  - **Step 3 (MAINTAIN PRESENT POSITION):** Splint and support joint strictly in the position it was found. Do NOT manipulate or realign.
  - **Step 4 (Warming & Shock Care):** Cover patient with warm dry blankets.
- **Bystander/Family Support:** Call emergency dispatch (115/911): *"Full-thickness major joint burn with exposed articular capsule/tendons"*.
- **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN (DO NOT DO):**
  - ⛔ ABSOLUTELY FORBIDDEN to forcefully extend or bend contracted joints (tears joint capsules and permanently severs tendons).
  - ⛔ DO NOT give oral food or fluids.
- **Medical Disposition:** **SURGICAL TRAUMA ORTHOPEDIC EMERGENCY.** Urgent transfer for surgical debridement, flap reconstruction, and articular preservation.

---

### REGION 9: PERINEUM & EXTERNAL GENITALIA
- **%TBSA (Prof. Le The Trung):** **1%** (Entire perineum, scrotum/vulva, and anal margin).
- **Clinical Hazards:** **Highest bacterial infection risk in human anatomy** (fecal/urinary flora contamination); rapid progressive urethral edema leading to **acute complete urinary retention** requiring emergency bladder catheterization.

#### Level 1: Mild (1st Degree Superficial, Redness on Groin Margin)
- **Calculated Burn Extent:** $< 0.5\%$ TBSA (isolated redness at upper inner thigh/groin fold).
- **Clinical Signs:** Faint redness along groin crease, stinging touch, zero blisters, smooth and painless micturition.
- **Real-World Scenarios:** Warm broth spilled on upper thigh edge near groin.
- **Step-by-Step Protocol:**
  - **Step 1 (Doff Underwear):** Remove underwear immediately to release heat.
  - **Step 2 (Gentle Irrigation):** Stream lukewarm/cool tap water gently over the area for 15–20 minutes using bidet spray or handheld shower.
  - **Step 3 (Dry):** Pat dry with clean towel.
  - **Step 4 (Extra-Loose Attire):** Wear very loose boxer shorts or wrap in a clean sarong; avoid tight underwear.
- **Bystander/Family Support:** Prepare loose, soft cotton clothing.
- **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN (DO NOT DO):**
  - ⛔ DO NOT apply rubbing alcohol or scented body sprays to perineal skin.
  - ⛔ DO NOT apply perfumed creams.
- **Medical Disposition:** Home observation.

---

#### Level 2: Moderate (2nd Degree, Blisters on Groin, Scrotum, or Labia Majora)
- **Calculated Burn Extent:** $0.5\% - 1\%$ TBSA of genitalia.
- **Clinical Signs:** Bullae on scrotum, labia, or inguinal creases; significant local edema; intense dysuria (burning sensation when urine touches excoriated skin); severe pain upon thigh adduction.
- **Real-World Scenarios:** Boiling instant noodle broth or hot tea tumbler dropped into lap while seated.
- **Step-by-Step Protocol:**
  - **Step 1 (Strip Lower Garments Immediately):** Cut away trousers and underwear immediately.
  - **Step 2 (Low-Pressure Water Irrigation 20 Minutes):** Direct a very gentle, smooth flow of cool tap water over the perineum for 20 minutes.
  - **Step 3 (EXPOSE TO AIR — DO NOT BANDAGE):** Leave exposed to air, draped lightly with a sterile moist gauze pad. NEVER APPLY ADHESIVE TAPES.
  - **Step 4 (INTER-THIGH GAUZE ROLL):** Place a soft sterile gauze roll between the inner thighs to prevent thigh friction against burned genitalia during movement.
- **Bystander/Family Support:** Gently rinse area with sterile normal saline after each voiding episode.
- **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN (DO NOT DO):**
  - ⛔ STRICTLY FORBIDDEN to apply tight dressings or adhesive tapes across perineum.
  - ⛔ DO NOT pop scrotal or labial blisters.
  - ⛔ DO NOT apply random antibiotic ointments or greasy salves.
- **Medical Disposition:** Mandatory hospital examination on the same day by Burn/Urology specialists for sterile dressing and urinary tract infection prophylaxis.

---

#### Level 3: Severe (Full-Thickness Genital Burn / Severe Edema / ACUTE URINARY RETENTION)
- **Calculated Burn Extent:** Deep dermal or full-thickness burn to perineum/genitalia.
- **Clinical Signs:** Gross grotesque swelling, charred black or sloughing genital tissue; **ACUTE COMPLETE URINARY RETENTION** (patient has painful full bladder urge but is physically unable to void due to severe inflammatory urethral occlusion); excruciating pain or sensory paralysis.
- **Real-World Scenarios:** Falling backward into basin of boiling scalding fluid; underwear catching fire and incinerating groin.
- **Step-by-Step Protocol:**
  - **Step 1 (CALL 115 / 911 REPORTING ACUTE URINARY RETENTION):** Dispatch EMS immediately. State: *"Severe genital burn with complete acute urinary retention requiring emergency urethral catheterization"*.
  - **Step 2 (Decontamination & Irrigation 5–10 Minutes):** Cut away all melted garment residues. Trickle cool clean water gently for 5–10 minutes to remove contaminants.
  - **Step 3 (Sterile Moist Gauze Drape):** Lay a sterile, saline-moistened gauze sheet loosely over the perineum. Keep patient supine with thighs slightly abducted.
  - **Step 4 (Keep Warm & RESTRICT FLUID INTAKE):** Cover chest and legs with dry warm blankets. **DO NOT GIVE LARGE AMOUNTS OF WATER** (drinking excess fluids while the urethra is fully blocked triggers agonizing bladder overdistension and risks bladder rupture).
- **Bystander/Family Support:** Provide emotional reassurance; enforce strict contamination control (shield wound from stool/soiling).
- **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN (DO NOT DO):**
  - ⛔ ABSOLUTELY FORBIDDEN to apply pressure dressings or bind legs together tightly.
  - ⛔ STRICTLY FORBIDDEN to squeeze, massage, or manipulate the urethra to force urination.
  - ⛔ DO NOT administer copious oral fluids or diuretic drinks while patient is in acute urinary retention.
- **Medical Disposition:** **SURGICAL UROLOGICAL EMERGENCY.** Rapid transfer to a Burn-Urology Center for **immediate Foley catheterization or suprapubic cystostomy** before the urethral lumen is completely occluded by edema. *(Pediatric cases: immediate transfer to Pediatric Burn Intensive Care).*

---

## PART 5: SYNOPTIC MATRIX: "MANDATORY ACTIONS" VS. "STRICTLY FORBIDDEN"

| Anatomical Region | Mandatory Core Actions (4 Steps) | STRICTLY FORBIDDEN Actions |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Head – Face – Neck** | Cool with gentle moist cloth $\rightarrow$ Loosen collar $\rightarrow$ Elevate head $30–45^\circ$ $\rightarrow$ Copious eye rinse | ⛔ **DO NOT** cover face with cling film.<br>⛔ **DO NOT** wrap circular bandages around neck. |
| **Upper Arms & Forearms**| Remove watches/rings $\rightarrow$ Irrigate 20 mins $\rightarrow$ Lay film longitudinally $\rightarrow$ Elevate above heart | ⛔ **DO NOT** spiral-wrap cling film around arm.<br>⛔ **DO NOT** rupture blisters. |
| **Hands & Fingers** | **Strip ALL rings within 5 mins** $\rightarrow$ Irrigate 20 mins $\rightarrow$ **Gauze between all digits** $\rightarrow$ Position of function | ⛔ **DO NOT** bind fingers together without spacers.<br>⛔ **DO NOT** forcefully unbend contracted digits. |
| **Anterior Torso (Chest)**| Cut clothing (never over head) $\rightarrow$ Cool moist towels $\rightarrow$ Warm legs/back $\rightarrow$ Semi-Fowler $30–45^\circ$ | ⛔ **DO NOT** pull hot clothes over head.<br>⛔ **DO NOT** submerge entire body in cold bath.<br>⛔ **DO NOT** give oral fluids if in respiratory shock. |
| **Posterior Torso (Back)**| Prone/lateral position $\rightarrow$ Cut shirt $\rightarrow$ Cool compresses $\rightarrow$ Drape clean sheet | ⛔ **DO NOT** allow patient to lie supine on burns.<br>⛔ **DO NOT** dump ice water over $> 15\%$ burns. |
| **Both Legs (Thigh/Calf)**| Cut off socks/shoes $\rightarrow$ Irrigate 20 mins $\rightarrow$ **Elevate leg on pillows** $\rightarrow$ Strict bed rest | ⛔ **DO NOT** permit patient to walk on injured leg.<br>⛔ **DO NOT** apply circular tight bandages. |
| **Feet & Toes** | Remove shoes/cut socks $\rightarrow$ Irrigate 20 mins $\rightarrow$ **Gauze between all toes** $\rightarrow$ Elevate 20 cm | ⛔ **DO NOT** wear tight shoes.<br>⛔ **DO NOT** permit bare toes to touch each other.<br>⛔ **DO NOT** bear weight or walk. |
| **Major Articulations** | Irrigate 20 mins $\rightarrow$ **Physiological neutral angle** (elbow $100^\circ$, knee extended) $\rightarrow$ Non-adherent cover | ⛔ **DO NOT** splint rigidly at abnormal angles.<br>⛔ **DO NOT** forcefully flex or extend joint. |
| **Perineum & Genitalia** | Remove underwear $\rightarrow$ Gentle water rinse $\rightarrow$ **Expose to air (never tape)** $\rightarrow$ **Gauze roll between thighs** | ⛔ **DO NOT** tape or bandage tightly.<br>⛔ **DO NOT** squeeze urethra to force urination.<br>⛔ **DO NOT** force oral fluids if in urinary retention. |
